gloss: to wash up on shore; to crash against; to surge in

definitions.gloss: to wash up on shore; to beat against; to break (of waves)
definitions.explanation: For waves to roll in and strike the shore, rocks, or a boat. Also used figuratively for crowds or emotions surging forward.

examples.english: The waves wash up on the shore.

examples.japanese: ⟦{大|おお}きな→大きな：02849_ookina⟧⟦{波|なみ}→波：00868_nami⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{岩場|いわば}→岩場：27478_iwaba⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{打|う}ち{寄|よ}せて⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: Big waves are crashing against the rocky shore.

examples.japanese: ⟦{台風|たいふう}→台風：01455_taifuu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{影響|えいきょう}→影響：01877_eikyou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧、⟦いつも→いつも：00599_itsumo⟧⟦より→より：09476_yori⟧⟦{高|たか}い→高い：00500_takai⟧⟦{波|なみ}→波：00868_nami⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{打|う}ち{寄|よ}せて⟦いた→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: Due to the typhoon, waves higher than usual were crashing in.

examples.japanese: ⟦ファン→ファン：10065_fan⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{歓声|かんせい}→歓声：02686_kansei⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{波|なみ}→波：00868_nami⟧⟦のように→のように：30291_noyouni⟧{打|う}ち{寄|よ}せた。
examples.english: The fans' cheers surged in like waves.

notes:
Compound of ⟦{打|う}つ→打つ：01221_utsu⟧ (to strike) + ⟦{寄|よ}せる→寄せる：02329_yoseru⟧ (to bring close). The literal sense — waves striking the shore — is by far the most common; figurative uses borrow the imagery of a wave.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{波|なみ}→波：00868_nami⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{打|う}ち{寄|よ}せる: waves wash up
- ⟦{浜辺|はまべ}→浜辺：17948_hamabe⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{打|う}ち{寄|よ}せる: to wash up on the beach
- ⟦{岩|いわ}→岩：00850_iwa⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{打|う}ち{寄|よ}せる: to crash against the rocks
- ⟦{波|なみ}→波：00868_nami⟧⟦のように→のように：30291_noyouni⟧{打|う}ち{寄|よ}せる: to surge in like waves

USAGE:
Most often appears in the present or て⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧ form, describing an ongoing scene. The subject is typically ⟦{波|なみ}→波：00868_nami⟧ (waves), but can be other things that move in wave-like motion.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{寄|よ}せる→寄せる：02329_yoseru⟧: to draw near — broader; the {打|う}ち prefix adds the impact nuance
- ⟦{押|お}し{寄|よ}せる→押し寄せる：06733_oshiyoseru⟧: to surge forward — emphasizes pressure or volume rather than the striking motion
